newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mostly firmer with futures.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mostly firmer with futures.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mostly firmer on Tuesday, traders said.

Gasoline was firmer as U.S. numbers rose and arbitrage opportunities were opening up not only from northwest Europe but also from the Med. A little buying interest for low octane barrels was seen into West Africa as well as Turkey and Lebanon.

West African interest was pegged at a discount of around $20 a tonne to premium quotes. A number of small pieces of Eurograde were seen available but overall the market is not particularly long, following refinery run cuts in the past couple of weeks.
Naphtha was firmer too, in response to rising crude.
Gas oil was strong and tight, epecially for low sulphur.

Traders said strong low sulphur prices -- premiums are put at Oct IPE +$18/+$19, basis Genoa -- had opened the arbitrage from North America and at least three cargoes were currently headed for the region.
Russian premiums were steady at quotes cif high +$2/+$3. Traders also said one player was trying to offload a 0.7 percent cargo out of Lavera, possibly into the bunker market.
The main Med low sulphur fuel oil buyer was understood to have bought a cargo on Monday, although this was unconfirmed.

Cargoes were seen steady around $116-119 cif NWE, gaining some support from a north European bid of $114.50 cif NWE for high viscosity product. With the contango into October still present sellers appear relaxed.
High sulphur cracked cargoes were divided between tight bunker quality supplies and slow enquiries for non-bunker spec.

A Turkish low sulphur buy tender was awarded today. A Tunisian high sulphur buy tender closes tomorrow. It consists of 200,000 tonnes, split between 65,000 tonnes of higher quality and 135,000 tonnes of lesser for delivery until January 1997.
